role: EntityGhast and the EntityLargeFireball it fires, over the an_world living and item pools: the ghast's old-AI wander, targeting and fireball attack, the fireball impact and explosion, ghast drops, and a bare probe player's damage paths, plus the probe's own World.updateEntities pass (gh_tick). Checked against the oracle's GhastProbe dump.
gpu: its former globals, function statics and lazily built tables are gone (lane/gpuenv, L2): per-environment state lives in struct env (csrc/engine/env.h), per-dimension state in the replay's dims, constant tables are built before main; csrc/tests/globals.sh lists what is left

line 216, function gh_closest_vulnerable_player: reads the gh_world through an->user_data (a void pointer only tests/test_ghasts.c sets), so a ghast outside the probe dereferences NULL (DEVLOG notes the play client crash)
line 318, function ghast_fire_fireball: calloc of an an_ent for every fireball inside the tick
function ghast_fire_fireball: the fireball joins the lists as pool slots and its shooter is an lref; a ghast's target is a flag on its world's player (lane/gpuarena, L3)
lines 517-540, function gh_expl_query: damage dispatched through function pointers (attack_from, add_motion)
line 598, function gh_fireball_impact: O(n) scan of an->list per new explosion item, and calloc per new an_ent (line 611)
line 730, function gh_player_attack_entity_from: while loop redrawing Math.random until the offset is non-degenerate (unbounded in principle)
lines 836-873, function ghast_collide_with_nearby_entities: result depends on chunk-section insertion order (container-order dependence, deliberate to match Java's double-add order)
line 953, function gh_spawn_ghast: calloc of the living and the an_ent
line 1054, function gh_tick: memmove removal from the list, order-dependent iteration with --i
notes: The probe player gh_player is a bare stand-in, not the real EntityPlayerMP; the fireball's flight lives in projectile.c (IE_LARGE_FIREBALL) and the explosion in explosion.c (expl_run_extras). Java member names for ghast fields (waypointX, targetedEntity, aggroCooldown, explosionStrength) were taken from the C field comments and MCP naming, not checked one by one against EntityGhast.java. The EntityGhast fireball-from-player reflect branch of attackEntityFrom is not ported (no probe source has a player attacker).
